html:
Southern Rhodesia was a self-governing British colony in what is now Zimbabwe, from 1923 until 1980. The map shows it in its 1938 snapshot.

When the rule of the British South Africa Company ended, white settlers voted in 1922 against joining South Africa and became a self-governing colony in 1923. Power lay with a small white minority. The Land Apportionment Act of 1930 set aside about half the land, including the best farmland, for whites, and pushed Africans into crowded reserves. Tobacco and gold were the main exports.

Southern Rhodesia led the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland from 1953 to 1963. When the others became independent under African rule, its white government under Ian Smith declared independence alone in 1965, as Rhodesia. A long guerrilla war followed, and in 1980 the country became Zimbabwe, led by Robert Mugabe.
